# 起信論疏

**Dynasty:** 新羅

## Contributors
- 元曉 (A000136)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-*juǎn* commentary on the *Dàshèng qǐxìn lùn* 大乘起信論 ([KR6o0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0078), the Liáng-Paramārtha translation, T32n1666), composed by the Silla Buddhist master [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686). Together with the *Qǐxìn lùn yìjì* of [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) [KR6o0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0105) and the lost commentary of Huìyuǎn 慧遠, this is one of the so-called *běnlùn sānshī* 本論三師 — the three foundational commentaries of the *Awakening of Faith* tradition. The *Sònggāosēng zhuàn* 宋高僧傳 attributes Wǒnhyo's reputation in Tang China largely to this very text: 法藏's pupil [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) is said to have learned the *Qǐxìn* tradition through Wǒnhyo's *shū* in the Huáinán region, and to have remarked that "this writing rises above all other masters'" (個書高出于諸師上者).

**Abstract**

The Taishō text is prefaced by an Edo-period 元祿 9 (1696) reprint preface, the *Qǐxìnlùn hǎidōngshū kānxíng xù* 起信論海東疏刊行序, signed by Juéyǎn 覺眼 of the Luòdōng Zhìjīmén 洛東智積門下 in Japan, who notes that of the three major commentaries on the *Qǐxìn lùn* — those of [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) Fǎzàng, Huìyuǎn, and Wǒnhyo — only the first two had circulated freely, while Wǒnhyo's was known only by name and reputation; the present 1696 edition was prepared from a manuscript that "some person" had brought to be carved and circulated.

The body of the *shū* opens with a famously elegant prologue of three "gates" (三門): (1) declaring the doctrinal substance (標宗體), (2) explaining the title (釋題名), and (3) elucidating the sense following the text itself (依文顯義). The opening characterization of the Mahāyāna ("luminously empty and still… so dark and so deep that it transcends the surface of myriad images, so still and still that it is yet found within the speech of the hundred schools…") is one of the most-quoted Buddhist passages in Korean literary history.

Wǒnhyo's interpretive program is to show that the *Qǐxìn lùn* synthesises Yogācāra and *Tathāgatagarbha* doctrine through the device of the "one mind opening into two gates" (一心開二門 *yīxīn kāi èrmén*) — the gate of true thusness (心真如門) and the gate of arising-and-perishing (心生滅門). This reading became canonical for the East-Asian *Qǐxìn* tradition; Fǎzàng's later *Yìjì* [KR6o0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0105) explicitly builds on Wǒnhyo's framework. The composition window is bracketed by Wǒnhyo's career, c. 650–686.

The Taishō establishes the text from the 元祿 9 / 1696 Japanese edition (原 = 原本), collated against the 大正 base.
